title: Fix in advance what gives way first
statement: Fix in advance the order in which a time-boxed lesson's parts give way for a slow learner: enrichment and untested items first, never what a later part depends on.
example: One design drops a 2:00 cloze with no test item behind it before a 0:40 device question the test assesses directly, buying three times the time.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design sets a ten-rung drop ladder for a slow child, starting with pure enrichment and then parts another step already covers or no test question stands behind, beside a list of parts never dropped whatever the clock says (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 351-418). The never-dropped list includes the taught word, because the independent write cashes it, and that write itself, the only unaided evidence the lesson produces. A revision moved a 2:00 cloze with no test item behind it ahead of a 0:40 device question the test assesses directly, since dropping it buys three times as much time (line 420).
against: The ladder is fitted to one design's lesson window (`g9/library/text/L8d5159.txt`, line 2).

evidence.quote: Two reasons: the cloze is 2:00 against the device MCQ at 0:40, so dropping it buys three times as much time, and the device MCQ is directly tested at 3.10(D) and 3.10(G) while the cloze has no STAAR item behind it at all.
When a child is slow, things give way in this order, first at the top. Ten rungs.
What is never traded: the read-aloud, the comprehension checks, the taught word, step 4 of the Modelling Moment, and Part 3.
Never dropped, whatever the clock says:
Part 3 cashes it. Drop this and Part 3 breaks.
The only unaided evidence the lesson produces.
